questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is a restriction endonuclease?
questions.solution:
Hind II is a type of restriction endonuclease.
A restriction enzyme or restriction endonuclease is an enzyme that cleaves DNA into fragments at or near specific recognition sites within the molecule known as restriction sites. Restrictions enzymes are one class of the broader endonuclease group of enzymes. Restriction enzymes are commonly classified into five types, which differ in their structure and whether they cut their DNA substrate at their recognition site, or if the recognition and cleavage sites are separate from one another. To cut DNA, all restriction enzymes make two incisions, once through each sugar-phosphate backbone (i.e. each strand) of the DNA double helix.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Bacteria acts as useful tool in biotechnology because of following reasons. The genetic code been universal; basic structure of genetic material is same. They are simple organisms, and easy to manipulate. Additionally, they multiply at a rapid rate.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium is natural gene transfer tool used by the bacteria to induce tumor into the host plant. The Ti plasmid is used as a vector to transfer the gene of interest into the plant and develop transgenic plant.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Plasmid is used as carrier because
options: Its both ends are replicating points
It can go between eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells
questions.solution: The plasmid is an extrachromosomal material in bacteria and is used in biotechnology or genetic engineering for making the multiple copies of desired genes (DNA segment). Plasmids are the carrier DNA molecules with antibiotic resistance gene. This feature makes it easy to isolate from the transformed cell with the desired insert in it.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A foreign gene is inserted in pBR322 using the restriction endonuclease EcoRI. Which of these is true about the E. coli having this pBR322?
options: It will be resistant to both antibiotic ampicillin as well as antibiotic tetracycline
It will be resistant to antibiotic ampicillin but not resistant to antibiotic tetracycline
It will be resistant to antibiotic tetracycline but not resistant to antibiotic ampicillin
It will be neither be resistant to antibiotic tetracycline nor to antibiotic ampicillin
questions.solution: The restriction site for EcoRI in pBR322 is not present within the ampicillin-resistant gene or within the tetracycline-resistant gene. Thus, when the foreign DNA is added, there will not be insertional activation of any of these genes and the bacterium will be resistant to both antibiotics.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Restriction enzymes, also called restriction nucleases (EcoRI in this question), surround the DNA molecule at the recognition point (sequence GAATTC for EcoRI). EcoRI cuts one strand of the DNA double helix at one point and the second strand at the complementary point (between the G and A base).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the column-I with column-II.
&
& Column-I & Column-II
$( A )$ Separation of DNA fragments $( P )$ Bioreactor
$( B )$ Separation and purification of products $( Q )$ Gel electrophoresis
$( C )$ Large scale production $( R )$ Downstream processing
questions.solution:
Downstream processing refers to the recovery and purification of biosynthetic products, particularly pharmaceuticals, from natural sources such as animal or plant tissue or fermentation broth.

A bioreactor may refer to any manufactured or engineered device or system that supports a biologically active environment. In one case, a bioreactor is a vessel in which a chemical process is carried out which involves organisms or biochemically active substances derived from such organisms.

Gel electrophoresis is a method for separation and analysis of macromolecules and their fragments, based on their size and charge.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding agarose gel electrophoresis and select the CORRECT ones.

I. The longest DNA fragment is nearest to the anode.
II. The matrix of the gel is a natural polymer obtained from sea-weeds.
III. The process is used to check the progression of restriction enzyme digestion.
IV. The fragments of DNA separate due to the sieving effect provided by agarose gel.
questions.solution: DNA fragments can be separated by a technique known as gel electrophoresis where molecules having a net negative charge migrate towards the positive electrode (anode), whereas net positively charged molecules migrate towards the negative electrode (cathode). The negatively charged DNA fragments are can be separated by forcing them to move towards the anode under an electric field through a medium/matrix (agarose, a natural polymer extracted from seaweeds). The larger fragments move slowly when compared to smaller ones and they tend to remain nearer to the cathode. The DNA fragments separate according to their size through the sieving effect provided by the agarose gel. The smaller fragment in size moves the farthest.& The process is used to check the progression of restriction enzyme digestion.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: This is the representation of pBR322 and all its restriction sites

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Two enzymes responsible for restricting the growth of bacteriophages in E.coli were isolated. One was methylase and other was a restriction endonuclease. What is the significance of methylase?
options: Able to cut the DNA of bacteriophage at specific site
Able to of remove the methyl group and hence prevent the action of restriction of endonuclease on host DNA
Protection of host DNA from the action of restriction endonuclease by adding methyl group to one or two bases usually within the sequences recognized by restriction enzyme
Able to ligate the two cohesive ends of DNA molecule
questions.solution: The host DNA is protected by other enzymes called methylases, which methylate adenine bases within host recognition sequences. For each restriction endonuclease, the host cell produces a corresponding methylase that marks the host DNA and prevents its degradation. These pairs of enzymes are referred to as restriction-modification systems.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The role of DNA ligase in the construction of a recombinant DNA molecule is
options: Formation of phosphodiester bond between sticky ends of DNA fragments
Formation of hydrogen bonds between sticky ends of DNA fragments
Ligation of all purine and pyrimidine bases
questions.solution: DNA ligase commonly called as genetic gum is used to join segments of DNA by forming phosphodiester bonds between 3' OH and 5' phosphate. Sticky and staggered ends facilitates the action of enzyme DNA ligase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is used in DNA fingerprinting?
questions.solution: DNA fingerprinting uses single-stranded radioactive probes that are washed over the nylon surface to allow their joining to any DNA fragments of the same composition thereby matching different DNA samples. Double-stranded probes would not hybridize with DNA fragments present on the nylon membrane.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: Restriction endonuclease is enzymes isolated from bacteria, are used to cut DNA at a specific location. They identify the specific palindromic regions in DNA at cuts at specific locations within the palindrome known as restriction sites by producing either sticky or blunt ends.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The polymerase chain reaction is a technique that
options: Is used for in vivo replication of DNA
Is used for in vivo synthesis of mRNA
Is used for in vitro synthesis of mRNA
Is used for in vitro replication of specific DNA sequence using thermostable DNA polymerase.
questions.solution: PCR is a technique in which a specific segment of DNA is replicated using taq DNA polymerase which is resistant to high temperature. PCR is based on principle that at high temperature double stranded DNA separates as single stranded DNA at a low temperature annealing occurs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Study the given diagram below of the stirred tank fermenter. What is the function of part labeled A?
options: To control the foam within the reactor
questions.solution: A stirred-tank reactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reactor contents. The stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor. The bioreactor has an agitator system, an oxygen delivery system, and a foam control system, a temperature control system, a pH control system, and sampling ports.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Statement I: Biolistics method of gene transfer is an example of direct gene transfer.

options: Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is true; Statement-2 is not the correct explanation of Statement-1.
Statement-1 is false, Statement-2 is true.
Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is false.
Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is true; Statement-2 is the correct explanation of Statement-1.
questions.solution: Biolistics is a commonly used method for genetic transformation of plants and other organisms. Millions of DNA-coated metal particles are shot at target cells or tissues using a biolistic device or gene gun.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Exonucleases, a type of nucleases that degrade nucleic acids, remove nucleotides from
questions.solution: Restriction enzymes belong to a larger class of enzymes called nucleases. They are of two types: exonucleases and endonucleases. Exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following option justify that why bacteria are useful in genetic engineering?
questions.solution:
Bacteria act as a useful tool in biotechnology because:

The genetic code has been universal, the basic structure of genetic material is the same. They are simple organisms and easy to manipulate; also, they multiply at a rapid rate. They have extrachromosomal DNA called plasmids which can be used as a vector in genetic engineering

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When we ligate a foreign DNA at the SalI site of pBR322, the ___a___ plasmid will lose tetracycline resistance due to the insertion of foreign DNA but can still be selected out from ___b___ ones by plating the ___c___ on ampicillin containing medium.
questions.solution: pBR322 is an& E.coli plasmid that contains origin of replication, ampicillin-resistant gene, tetracycline resistance gene, and multiple cloning site. It is a highly studied plasmid vector. Because it has two resistance genes, transformed cells can be screened from non-transformed by process of insertional inactivation in which target DNA when inserted into tetracycline gene, disrupt the gene and making cell recombinant with resistance to ampicillin only. Hence, colonies formed on the ampicillin plate are those which contain target DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following restriction endonucleases cannot be used while using pBR322 as a cloning vector?
questions.solution: pBR322 has two restriction sites BamHI (from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens) and SalI (from Streptomyces albus) on the tetracycline-resistant gene (tetR), which acts as a selectable marker. It also has two restriction sites PstI (from Providenciastuartii) and PvuI (from Proteus vulgaris)& on ampicillin-resistant gene (ampR), which also acts as a selectable marker. Hence, these four enzymes can be used. however, the restriction site for PvuII is present on rop (replication of plasmid) region. If used, it will interfere with the process of replication of plasmid.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The basic components of a PCR reaction includes&
questions.solution: The basic components of a PCR reaction are a DNA template, short RNA or DNA primers, nucleotides (dNTP's), Taq polymerase (DNA polymerase), and a buffer. The DNA template usually is the sample DNA, which needs to be amplified.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
There are three basic steps in creating genetically modified organisms. Arrange these steps in the correct sequence.

$\left(a.\right)$ Introduction of the identified DNA into the host
$\left(b.\right)$ Maintenance of introduced DNA in the host and transfer of the DNA to its progeny
$\left(c.\right)$ Identification of DNA with desirable genes
questions.solution: To modify any organism genetically, desired gene of interest is identified and isolated; the gene is then inserted into the desired host using the suitable method at such a position that the gene multiplies into the host and is transferred to all the progeny cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When a viral DNA is incorporated inside the host DNA, it is known as:
questions.solution: In virus showing temperate or lysogenic cycle viral DNA gets intergrated into host DNA and is transmitted as such to next generation, such viral DNA is called prophage.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Elution is
questions.solution: Using gel electrophoresis the DNA fragments are separated according to their size on gel block in the electric field. If the gel block is cut to remove the DNA fragments than the process is called elution.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statement/s is/are an example of genetic engineering?

I. Inserting a gene for human insulin production into bacteria.
II. Selective breeding to produce cattle with high milk yields.
III. Using methods like crop rotation with leguminous plants to increase the fertility of the soil.
IV. Vegetative propagation and grafting are practised to ensure higher yield.
questions.solution: Techniques to alter the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA), to introduce these into host organisms and thus change the phenotype of the host organism come under genetic engineering. Statement I is only one where the gene is been manipulated artificially to get the desired effect. Selective breeding can be considered as gene manipulation but there is no control on the outcome but chance.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The efficiency of the cell to take up rDNA is increased by
questions.solution:
Divalent cation like calcium increases the permeability of bacterial cell wall for DNA so that the DNA readily enters the cell.

In order to force bacteria to take up the plasmid, the bacterial cells must first be made ‘competent’ to take up DNA. This is done by treating them with a specific concentration of a divalent cation, such as calcium, which increases the efficiency with which DNA enters& the bacterium through pores in its cell wall. Recombinant DNA can then be forced into such cells by incubating the cells with recombinant DNA on ice, followed by placing them briefly at 42& ^{0}C (heat shock) and then putting them back on ice. This enables the bacteria to take up the recombinant DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Production on an industrial scale requires growing microbes in very large vessels is called
questions.solution: Fermentor are large vessels in which the desired microbes can be cultured to obtain specific product in large quantity. Fermentors are used for production of alcoholic beverage and for production of specific antibiotics.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Restriction endonuclease HindII acts on a palindromic specific sequence of.............. base pair.
questions.solution: HindII was the first restriction enzyme to be discovered from bacteria Haemophilus influenza. It identifies specific $\text{6 bp}$ long palindromic DNA segments and cuts at specific locations within the sequence.

questions.solution: Plasmids are extrachromosomal self-replicating DNA present in the cytoplasm of bacteria. The given plasmid is pBR322, the most common vector used in genetic engineering.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is part of bioprocess engineering?
questions.solution:
The two core techniques that enabled the birth of modern biotechnology are
(i) Genetic engineering: It involves the techniques to alter the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA) to introduce these into host organisms and thus change the phenotype of the host organism.
(ii) Bioprocess engineering: It is the process of maintaining sterile ambience in chemical engineering processes to enable the growth of only the desired microbe/eukaryotic cell in large quantities for the manufacture of biotechnological products like antibiotics, vaccines, enzymes, etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following represents the steps involved in developing GMOs?
options: Introduction of identified $\text{DNA}$ into the host.
Maintenance of introduced $\text{DNA}$ in the host and transfer of the $\text{DNA}$ to its progeny.
questions.solution: For genetically modifying an organism, a specific desired gene needs to be isolated. This desired gene should be introduced in a specific host cell, where it can multiply and get transferred to all the progeny cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Electroporation is a technique that can be used for genetic engineering. This technique enables gene manipulation by
options: Opening of stomatal pores during night by artificial light
Purification of saline water with the assist of a membrane system
Making transient pores in cell membrane to introduce gene constructs
Fast passage of food through sieve pores in phloem elements with the help of electric stimulation
questions.solution: Electroporation is the process where electric energy is passed through living tissue surface causing appearance of pores on the membrane, which then can be used to pass the biological material easily. This way we can introduce the gene of interest.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the reason for using restriction endonucleases as a tool for genetic engineering?
questions.solution: An endonuclease is a biocatalyst protein that is able to identify a specific, short nucleotide sequence, and it makes cuts at that site of the DNA sequence. DNA sequencing pattern is the same in all organisms known to contain DNA as genetic material. Thus, these enzymes can act as a cutter for desired DNA sequence coding for a particular gene which then can be placed in the genome of the desired organism. The DNA fragments can be joined by enzyme DNA ligase. Restriction endonucleases do not act on protein; rather, they act on DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the criterion for DNA fragments movement on agarose gel during gel electrophoresis?
questions.solution:
Gel electrophoresis was developed by Tiselius and is based on the principal that charged molecules move to electrode of opposite charge when placed in electric field and the movement depends on the charge and size of the molecule.
Due to the sieve-like texture of the gel, smaller DNA fragments travel faster toward the electrode than the larger fragments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Stirred-tank bioreactors have been designed for
options: addition of preservatives to the product
availability of oxygen throughout the process
ensuring anaerobic conditions in the culture vessel
questions.solution: A stirred-tank reactor is usually cylindrical or with a curved base to facilitate the mixing of the reactor contents. The stirrer facilitates even mixing and oxygen availability throughout the bioreactor.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: The desired product has to be subjected through a series of processes before it is ready for marketing as a finished product, once the biosynthetic stage has completed. The processes include separation and purification, which are collectively referred to as downstream processing.

A recombinant $\text{DNA}$ is inserted within the coding sequence of enzyme $\beta -$ galactosidase. This results in insertational inactivation, and the colonies do not produces any colour.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.solution: $\text{pBR322}$ is the first plasmid vector developed by Bolivar and Rodrigues to transfer gene of interest to desire host cell. BamHI, SalI and EcoRII are restriction endonucleases, which are used to cut specific DNA segments.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The technique polymerase chain reaction was developed by ________.
questions.solution:
Polymerase chain reaction, also known as gene amplification, was developed by Kary B. Mullis to make multiple copies of specific DNA in an artificial medium. PCR can detect the pathogens (bacteria or virus) at very low concentrations by the amplification of nucleic acids even before the development of the symptoms. Few uses of PCR:

(i) PCR can detect HIV in suspected patients of AIDS.

(ii) PCR can detect mutations in genes in suspected patients of cancer.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Denaturation is a step in the procedure called Polymerase Chain Reaction. This step does not involve which of the following process?
options: Breaking of hydrogen bonds of the original DNA double helix
Addition of nucleotides to the primer by DNA polymerase
questions.solution: PCR stands for Polymerase Chain Reaction. In this reaction, gene (segment of DNA) of interest is synthesized in vitro and multiple copies are generated. The main steps of PCR- Denaturation - where the double-stranded template DNA is heated to separate it into two single strands. Annealing - where the temperature is lowered to enable the DNA primers to attach to the template DNA. Extension - where the temperature is raised and the new strand of DNA is made by the Taq polymerase enzyme.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following shows the correct sequence of processes with respect to the PCR?
questions.solution: PCR stands for a polymerase chain reaction, in this reaction, multiple copies of the gene of interest are synthesized in vitro using two sets of primers and enzyme $\text{DNA}$ polymerase. The enzyme extends the primers using the nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic $\text{DNA}$ as a template. It involves denaturation of the $\text{DNA}$, attachment of primers called annealing and extension by enzyme $\text{DNA}$ polymerase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Correct statement about restriction endonuclease.

(I) It is the enzyme which cuts $\text{DNA at}$ a particular point.
(II) The first restriction endonuclease was $\text{HindII.}$
(III) Overall, $\text{900}$ restriction enzymes have been isolated from about $\text{200}$ strains.
(IV) Each restriction endonuclease recognizes a specific palindromic sequence.
options: I, II, and IV are correct.
questions.solution: The first restriction endonuclease HindII whose functioning ws found to be dependent on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence was isolated and characterized 5 years later. It was found that HindII always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point by recognizing a specific sequence of six base pairs. This specific base sequence is known as the recognition sequence for HindII. Besides Hind II, today we know more than 900 restriction enzymes that have been isolated from over 230 strains of bacteria, each of which recognizes different recognition sequences. Each restriction endonuclease recognizes a specific palindromic sequence.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Analyze the statements given below regarding the thermal cycler and select the option that shows incorrect statements.

I. Annealing is also called the hybridization of oligonucleotide (primer).
II. During extension, $DNA$ polymerase polymerizes nucleotides in $5′ \to 3′$ direction.
III. Denaturation is a process of formation of H-bonds.
questions.solution: The pairing of denatured $DNA$ upon cooling is known as annealing. In PCR, the synthesis of nucleotide chain proceeds in $5′ \to 3′$ direction. PCR stands for polymerase chain reaction. In this reaction, multiple copies of the gene (or DNA) of interest are amplified.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Selectable marker is associated with
questions.solution: Due to the presence of the selective marker, the plasmid becomes useful for the cell. Under the selective conditions, only cells that contain plasmids with the appropriate selectable marker can survive. Commonly, genes that confer resistance to various antibiotics are used as selective markers in cloning vectors.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following can be used to insert the recombinant DNA into the animal cell?
questions.solution: Microinjection is a technique of delivering foreign DNA into a living cell (a cell, egg, oocyte or embryos of animals) through a glass micropipette. $2$ Agrobacterium tumefaciens $II$ $pBR322$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: DNA fingerprinting is a technique used in generating a profile of an individual. This technique identifies the various satellite DNA found in the sequence and has high degree of
questions.solution: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in a DNA sequence called satellite DNA. These sequences of satellite DNA normally do not code for any proteins and they show a high degree of polymorphism which forms the basis of DNA fingerprinting. Polymorphism is the ability to take any form or change in sequence (viz., SNP). Metamorphism is the phenomenon of the transition of certain animal groups from the larval stage to the adult stage. (viz. tadpole to frog). Pathomorphism is a term given for abnormal morphology shown in any part of body and biomorphism is an art form imitating the living organisms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Sticky ends, observed in the DNA, are due to the action of a particular type of nucleases. Which of the following statement is correct regarding the sticky ends of the DNA strand?
options: The sticky ends are made of unpaired nucleotides
The sticky ends have an adhesive group for attachment.
The sticky ends are made of paired up nucleotides
The sticky ends are made by the action of ligases
questions.solution: Restriction endonucleases are a group of nucleases that break the phosphodiester bond in the DNA that result in a 'cut' in the DNA strand and separation. These enzymes cut the DNA at a particular site and may leave single stranded portions at the ends. These overhanging stretches of unpaired nucleotides are called sticky ends.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these statements about Taq polymerase used during PCR is not correct?
options: It is used for primer extension to synthesise a new DNA strand
It is a thermostable enzyme and can survive temperatures up to ${125}^{o}C$
Its addition eliminated the need to add fresh polymerase in every PCR cycle
questions.solution: Taq polymerase is a thermostable DNA polymerase found in thermophilic bacteria& Thermus aquaticus. Its optimum temperature for activity is approx. $75 – 80°C$. Taq polymerase is well-suited for PCR because it is able to withstand the temperature of up to $95°C$ required for DNA strand separation without denaturing.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Sequences of DNA can be removed from a genome with the help of
questions.solution: Restriction enzymes are also called as molecular scissors as these enzymes have the ability to cut DNA at specific sites. These enzymes also called endonucleases cut the DNA within the sequence and this feature is useful as a genetic tool for developing genetically modified organisms. Ligases help in joining strands of DNA.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: There are certain sequences of DNA that are termed as mobile or jumping genes and are useful as vectors. Such sequences are called as
questions.solution: Transposons are DNA sequences that have the ability to move within the genome. Such changes in the position can make or remove mutations even altering the genetic identity of the genome. This ability can be harnessed as a vector to insert genes of our choice into the host genome.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The prokaryote that is credited with construction of the first recombinant DNA by linking an antibiotic resistance gene with its native plasmid is
questions.solution: The construction of the first recombinant DNA by linking a gene encoding antibiotic resistance with a native plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium was accomplished in 1972 by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The process of recovery and purification of the expressed biological products is called
questions.solution: After completion of the biosynthetic stage, the product has to be subjected through a series of processes before it is ready for manufacturing as a finished product. The processes include separation and purification, which are referred to as downstream processing.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What does 'R' in EcoRI represent?
questions.solution: The convention for naming the restriction enzymes is the first letter of the name comes from the genus and the second and the third letters come from the species of the prokaryotic cell from which they were isolated. In EcoRI, the letter 'R' is derived from the name of the strain. The roman number indicates the order in which the enzyme was isolated from the strain of bacteria.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If pBR322 cloning vector is cut by Pvu I enzyme for the formation of rDNA then which of its marker gene helps in the selection of recombinants?
questions.solution: pBR 322 has two selectable markers which are amphicillin and tertacyclin resistant genes. Amphicilin resistant gene has two restriction enzyme recognition site, Pvu I and Pst I. If the vector is cut by Pvu I enzyme for formation of rDNA than amphicillin resistant gene becomes inactive due to insertional inactivation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A plasmid has accepted the gene of interest, such as gene coding for streptomycin. How can we make clones of this plasmid?
options: Inserting it into a virus to generate multiple copies
Treating it with a restriction enzyme in order to cut the molecule into small pieces
Inserting it into a suitable bacterium in order to produce multiple copies
Running it on a gel electrophoresis in order to determine the size of the gene of interest
questions.solution: Plasmid is an extra-chromosomal DNA found in bacteria which can self-replicate. To make multiple copies of a plasmid (a small circular DNA), it should be inserted into a bacterium. A plasmid would not replicate if it were inserted into a virus, as viruses do not contain plasmid and don't have the necessary conditions for its replication. Treating the plasmid with a restriction enzyme will cut into smaller fragments, rendering the plasmid useless. Running the plasmid on a gel (using gel electrophoresis) would only tell us the size of the plasmid and not make clones or copies.

In genetic engineering, after the creation of recombinant DNA, it has to be transferred into the host using a vector. Which of the following agents can be used as a vector?

A. pBR322
B. E.coli
C. Transposons
D. Mosquito
E. A disarmed Ti plasmid
options: A, B, C, D, and E
questions.solution: Plasmids and bacteriophages are commonly used vectors. The vector should have a few (or) at least one unique recognition site to link the foreign/alien DNA. Transposons are also frequently used as cloning vectors (the bacteriophage lambda is important in molecular biology because it is used in constructing vectors for gene cloning. Plasmids do this as well, but bacteriophages have an advantage over plasmids. Plasmids are circular, independently replicating, double-stranded DNA, most often found in bacteria. They replicate quickly and are easily manipulated in the laboratory. Plasmids are typically 2-10 thousand base pairs in size (Corbley, 1999). While this small size allows plasmids the two aforementioned attributes, it also means that plasmids are limited in the DNA fragments they can clone. They are typically limited to fragments around 5 thousand base pairs (King, 2002). While plasmids are great vector vehicles for many molecular endeavours, if the fragment to be cloned is larger than the available insertion space of the plasmid, the plasmid vector will probably not transfer the fragment of DNA successfully). Disarmed retroviruses are used as vectors in animals.

questions.q: In the polymerase chain reaction, the optimum temperature for the extension step is
questions.solution:
A single PCR reaction involves three temperature-dependent steps, described as follows:
i) Denaturation: The starting solution is heated, usually to 94oC. The high temperatures break the hydrogen bonds between the two strands of the original DNA double helix, providing the necessary single-stranded templates.
ii) Annealing: After just a couple of minutes at that temperature, the reaction mixture is quickly cooled, usually to somewhere between 50oC and 60oC. It is then held for less than a minute at this lower temperature which is enough time for the primers to bind to their complementary sequences on the single-stranded templates.
iii) Primer extension (polymerization): The sample is next heated to 72oC for some time, during which time the DNA polymerase adds nucleotides to the primer, synthesizing a new DNA strand using only the template sequences that bind the primers.
